name: Jordà-Schularick-Taylor Macrohistory Database
description: A long-run macroeconomic and financial dataset for 18 advanced economies from 1870 to the present, assembled by Òscar Jordà, Moritz Schularick and Alan M. Taylor (hosted by the MacroFinance & MacroHistory Lab at the Kiel Institute, led by Schularick). Covers real economy, credit, house price, asset return and financial crisis variables previously dispersed across many national sources.

notes: Also distributed as Stata .dta (JSTdatasetR6.dta), including a direct `use` URL for loading into Stata without downloading first.
One workbook covering all 18 countries and all 48 variables, annual observations, no API.

terms.summary: Free download for non-commercial (e.g. academic) use under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International; commercial data providers may not integrate or resell it; requires attribution/citation and identical (ShareAlike) licensing of derivatives
terms.quote: Commercial data providers are thus strictly forbidden to integrate all or parts of the dataset into their services and/or resell the data.

datasets.name: JST Macrohistory Database, Release 6 (R.6)
datasets.gives: 48 annual variables per country: real GDP, consumption, investment, unemployment, wages; current account, trade, exchange rates; government revenue/expenditure/debt; money supply, short- and long-term interest rates, consumer prices; total/mortgage/household/business bank loans; house prices; financial crisis dates; equity, housing, bond and bill total returns; exchange-rate peg status; bank capital and balance-sheet ratios
datasets.units: percent, index, national currency, ratio (varies by variable)
notes: Release R.6 (2022) is the latest of an irregular release series (R1 through R6); no dated release-history page was found, so the cadence between releases is 'irregular' at the file level, not a fixed schedule.
18 countries (advanced economies only, ~90% of advanced-economy output, >50% of world output as of R.6); Ireland was the most recent addition per the database page.

Citation is per-variable-group, not one blanket citation: Jordà/Schularick/Taylor 2017 for general use, Jordà/Knoll/Kuvshinov/Schularick/Taylor 2019 for returns data, and Jordà/Richter/Schularick/Taylor 2021 for bank balance-sheet ratios; the page also asks users to note the consultation date since statistics are subject to revision.
Not yet used by any series/*.json descriptor as of 2026-09-15 — roadmap only.

verified.by: Claude (S9 workflow agent jst-macrohistory): read https://www.macrohistory.net/database/ (license, citations, downloads), https://www.macrohistory.net/data/ (release/download URLs), and https://www.macrohistory.net/ (homepage/nav)

notes: No public API; single workbook/Stata-file download covering the whole database, not per-variable or per-country files.

terms.status is restricted (not verified) because the CC BY-NC-SA licence forbids commercial use/resale — this repo publishes republished values on a public page, so any future use of this data needs the non-commercial and attribution/ShareAlike conditions checked against how the value would be shown, not assumed compatible by default.
